tracking.indicator: Risk Assessment and Adaptation Planing for Heritage Places
tracking.findings: Custodians of these heritage places have now mapped relevant rightsholders and stakeholders and engaged them in a locally led climate change risk assessment and adaptation planning process for their heritage place and are in the process of disseminating the results. These heritage places include Petra Archaeology Park (Jordan), the Historic Mosque City of Bagerhat (Bangladesh), Payo'n Binoltan - Ifugao Rice Terraces (Philippines) and Nelson’s Dockyard National Park (Antigua and Barbuda).

tracking.findings: Cooperation has taken place in the UNFCCC processes to raise the issue of ECD and climate change at the international level. This has resulted in children being identified as a uniquely vulnerable population in the Belém Health Action Plan. Work will continue with these processes to seek further opportunities to raise the topic and to support countries in making domestic adaptation policies.

cases.title: Contribution to Belem Health Action Plan
cases.initiative: by the Children and Climate Initiative
cases.target: Related CCI targets: Domestic policy development; International awareness raising
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 16. Promoting resilient health systems.
body: The Children and Climate Initiative collaborated with the Brazilian Health Ministry to provide evidence and refined wording to ensure children were identified as a uniquely vulnerable demographic in the Belem Health Action Plan (BHAP). The resulting document requires signatories to design adaptive health policy which accurately reflects their needs.

Subsequently, the CCI was invited to join Action Group 16 on resilient health systems and WHO's ATACH community. Signatory countries must now address children as a uniquely vulnerable group and shape their health sector adaptation plans to fit their needs.
The Initiative’s overall goals include awareness raising and facilitating policy change to reflect the interests of children – this outcome is specifically related to achieving this goal.

cases.title: Onboarding 2026 Cohort of Heritage Custodians
body: Preserving Legacies is on a mission to safeguard the world’s heritage places and practices from the impacts of climate change by supporting local change makers with training, tools, and connections to equitably adapt what their communities cherish most and build a more just and thriving future.

Preserving Legacies is welcoming the custodians of seven new heritage places and practices to the Preserving Legacies climate adaptation program, each bringing their distinct histories, perspectives, skills, and relationships to the shared challenge of climate change: Engaresero GIAHS Site (Ngorongoro District, Tanzania); Kci-peskiyak (Sipayik, Maine, USA); Lahemaa National Park (Estonia); Lamu Old Town (Lamu Island, Kenya); Mount Wutai (Shanxi, China); Mosi-Oa-Tunya / Victoria Falls (Livingstone, Zambia); Palestine: Land of Olives and Vines – Cultural Landscape of Southern Jerusalem – Battir (Battir, Bethlehem, Palestine).

As Foundation Sites, this cohort will spend their first year strengthening climate and cultural literacy, preparing for values-based risk assessments, and building the groundwork for long-term adaptation action.

They are joining 30 heritage places and practices in different phases of the initiative’s flagship three-year climate adaptation cohort program, which supports local custodians with the tools, training, and networks needed to design and implement values-based climate adaptation strategies. Grounded in principles that are community-led, values-driven, science-informed, and open-access, the program supports communities to protect what they value most.
